root_motivation: Grounding: opportunity from visions/mcphost-aistack-harvest.md (WWHTBT leaf 1 and weakest link leaf 2). host.table.query returns a JSON array of rows and nothing else (src/tables.rs:725); a model describing those rows in prose is doing its own unverified arithmetic, and mcphost serves no HTML a chart could live on. ai-stack already has a tested, grammar-free chain (mqo-chart-recommender, mqo-vega-emitter, mqo-chart-caption, mqo-chart-vocab, mqo-result-profiler) that turns a typed column profile plus rows into a chart recommendation, a Vega-Lite spec, and a caption whose numbers are computed from the data, not guessed. This build vendors that chain, writes the one missing piece (a profiler that reads SQL rows instead of an MQO response, reusing src/tables_model.rs's existing classifiers), and exposes host.table.chart(sql) plus a signed share link so a spreadsheet owner can see the picture and hand it to a teammate.
user_persona: The spreadsheet owner from the database recipe: a table on mcphost, a Claude client, no BI tool. After a question they want to see the answer as a chart and paste one sentence about it into a message, without trusting a model's own arithmetic.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the vendored crates in vendor/, When the gate runs, Then their own test suites pass unchanged and vendor/VENDOR.md names source repo and commit.

Given the 1,000-row fixture, When host.table.chart runs SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS total FROM expenses GROUP BY category, Then the profile has one nominal dimension and one quantitative measure, the recommendation mark is a bar, and the spec's data.values holds five rows.
Given the same result, When the caption is read, Then its headline names the fixture's largest category and every fact's value equals a value recomputed from the rows in the test.

Given SELECT day, SUM(amount) FROM expenses GROUP BY day, When chart runs, Then is_temporal is true for day only if it parses as a date; for the integer day column the mark is a bar, and for an ISO-date column in a second fixture table the mark is a line.
Given a query returning zero rows, When chart runs, Then mark is Table, vega_lite.data.values is empty, and the caption headline is the no-takeaway text.
Given SELECT COUNT(*) FROM expenses, When chart runs, Then mark is BigNumber and the caption headline states the count.
Given mark: "pie" when the alternatives do not include it, When chart runs, Then a validation error names the allowed marks and no chart is stored.
Given share: true, When the returned share_url is fetched without any auth header, Then 200 with HTML containing the spec inline and the caption headline, and no tenant id or key appears in the body.
Given a share URL past its expiry or with an altered signature, When fetched, Then 410 or 403 respectively and no chart body.
Given 100 stored charts, When a 101st is shared, Then the oldest is gone and host.table.charts lists 100.
Given a python tool calling mcphost.table.chart(sql), When it runs in the sandbox, Then it receives the same chart.v1 object the tool returns.

Given prod after land, When examples/chart-in-a-minute/proof.sh https://mcphost.dev/mcp runs from carbon with a fresh signup, Then it exits 0 in under 30s, the caption's largest-category fact matches the fixture, and the share URL returns 200.
acceptance_criteria.test: DEFERRED: operator-provisioned (Live, prod after deploy, requires a real box and a deploy this dispatch cannot provision)

acceptance_criteria.description: Given www/llms.txt, When the chart section is read, Then it is under 50 lines and shows one chart call and one share link and no grammar other than SQL.
Given ten concurrent chart calls for one tenant, When they finish, Then all ten return chart.v1 and p95 latency on the builder is under 250ms.

scope: vendor/{mqo-chart-vocab,mqo-result-profiler,mqo-chart-recommender,mqo-vega-emitter,mqo-chart-caption}/: five crates vendored unchanged as path dependencies, vendor/VENDOR.md records source repo (~/projects/ai-stack) and commit (4ef6c22).

src/chart.rs (new): builds a result-profile.v1 value from a SQL query's columns and rows (reusing src/tables_model.rs's key/category/measure/date classifiers, made pub(crate) for this), host.table.chart/host.table.charts tool implementations, signed share-link minting and verification, and the /charts/{id} HTML handler.

migrations/0057_chart_index.sql, src/db.rs: a tenant-agnostic chart_index table in the main mcphost.db routing an unauthenticated GET /charts/{id} to the right tenant's own SQLite file, where the chart body itself lives in a new _mcphost_charts table.

src/handler.rs, src/http.rs, src/kinds/python.rs, src/kinds/mod.rs: host.table.chart/host.table.charts tool descriptors and dispatch, the /charts/{id} route, and the mcphost.table.chart python sandbox bridge function.
www/llms.txt: new "Chart in a minute" recipe section. examples/chart-in-a-minute/: fixture.csv, proof.sh, synthorg-task.yaml, mirroring the database-in-a-minute precedent.
Cargo.toml/CHANGELOG.md: version bump 0.62.0 -> 0.63.0 (PRD's own build_version_bump: minor rule) and a CHANGELOG entry recording the feature and AC12's deferral.

tests/chart_ac01..14 (AC12 has no test file, recorded deferred): one integration test file per non-deferred AC, tests/support/chart_fixture.rs holding the shared 1,000-row expenses fixture and small events fixture.
non_goals: Server-side rendering to PNG or SVG -- the share page renders in the browser (PRD's own non-goal).
A charts gallery or dashboard composition -- mqo-dashboard-composer is not vendored.
Editing a recommendation's encoding -- the caller may only override mark, from the recommender's own alternatives.
Any query grammar beyond sql -- PRD's own non-goal, confirmed by AC13's test that the recipe section shows no grammar other than SQL.

additional.test_file_names_use_underscores_not_the_: test_prefix chart (the PRD's own frontmatter field), same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.crate_layout_stays_one_package: mcphost is one package with [lib] and [[bin]] (Cargo.toml:11); vendored crates are path dependencies under vendor/ picked up by Cargo's implicit-workspace rule, not a workspace conversion -- deny.toml and clippy.toml apply to them unchanged.
additional.charts_stored_per_tenant_not_centrally: _mcphost_charts lives inside each tenant's own SQLite file (tables::tenant_db_path), matching every other host.table.* table; only a small global chart_index (new migration 0057) in the main mcphost.db routes an unauthenticated /charts/{id} request, which has no tenant in its URL, to the right tenant file.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does mcphost need its own profiler instead of reusing mqo-result-profiler::profile directly?
five_whys_trace.a: mqo-result-profiler's profile(response, catalog) reads an MQO response shape ai-stack's other services produce; host.table.chart has a SQL query's columns and rows instead, so src/chart.rs builds the result-profile.v1 value itself, vendoring mqo-result-profiler only for its ResultProfile/ColumnProfile/MeasureRange types (PRD's own explicit instruction).

five_whys_trace.q: Why reuse src/tables_model.rs's classifiers instead of writing new measure/dimension thresholds for the chart profiler?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD requirement 2 says so explicitly ("Role decisions reuse the classifiers in src/tables_model.rs rather than new thresholds") -- mcphost already has tested key/category/measure/date/id classifiers from the table-semantic-model PRD; a second set of thresholds would drift from them silently over time.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC12 get deferred rather than attempted against the real https://mcphost.dev?
five_whys_trace.a: AC12 is explicitly a Live acceptance criterion ("Given prod after land") requiring a deploy that has not happened yet and a run from carbon (the real operator's box) -- this dispatch works only in an isolated git worktree against a remote build-and-test runner, with no authority to deploy or provision production infrastructure, so it is recorded deferred as operator-provisioned rather than faked against a local stand-in.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is AC14's concurrency/latency test run against the in-process TestServer rather than a subprocess on a fixed reference box, the way the repo's other hardware-dependent AC (ac11_load_smoke) is?
five_whys_trace.a: AC14's own bound (250ms p95 for 10 concurrent in-process chart calls) is two orders of magnitude looser than ac11_load_smoke's 50ms bound for 200 real-subprocess calls measuring RSS; an in-process TestServer run (0.37s total wall time observed) already clears that bound with wide margin and needs no subprocess isolation, so it runs unconditionally in the gate instead of being #[ignore]d for manual hardware-specific runs.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 5's examples/chart-in-a-minute/ directory has no dedicated AC number in the PRD's acceptance-criteria list (AC13 only covers the llms.txt section) -- does it still need its own delivered proof?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes -- delivered as its own commit (fixture.csv matching tests/support/chart_fixture.rs::expenses_rows() exactly, proof.sh, synthorg-task.yaml) per the PRD's requirement 5 text, verified by actually building the mcphost binary and running proof.sh against it end to end (exit 0, ~1.3s wall time) rather than only checking the script parses.

ambiguities_resolved.question: requirement 3 says host.table.chart(sql, title?, mark?) but P1 requirement 6 adds share: true -- is share part of the same tool or a separate one?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Same tool, one additional optional argument (share: bool), consistent with requirement 6's own description of share as part of the host.table.chart call and with the python bridge's signature in requirement 7 (mcphost.table.chart(sql, title=None, mark=None, share=False)).
